candidates.source_name: ČNB – Pravidla platebního systému CERTIS (rules page)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative, versioned operating rules for CERTIS issued by ČNB under §112 of Act 370/2017 Sb.; binds every CZ interbank participant and carries dated effective dates (Version 14 effective 19 May 2025 seen in results). Rule changes = dated obligations for banks and their vendors.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML fetch of the page + diff on linked PDF filenames (which encode effective dates, e.g. pravidla_CERTIS_od_20250519.pdf); download and version each PDF.
queries_used: ČNB CERTIS pravidla pro účastníky mezibankovního platebního systému

candidates.source_name: ČNB – CERTIS section hub (Popis systému CERTIS)
candidates.why_relevant: Hub linking rules, technical annexes, instant-payments scheme description, participant lists and the Registr pro platby na kontakt; best single snowball point for CERTIS-related obligations.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the section tree monthly; extract child page URLs and PDF links.
queries_used: ČNB CERTIS pravidla pro účastníky mezibankovního platebního systému

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Okamžité platby (instant payments scheme pages)
candidates.why_relevant: Describes the CZK instant-payments scheme rules layered on CERTIS: voluntary adherence but mandatory receipt up to CZK 2.5m per payment and a 10-second technical standard. These are contractual scheme obligations, not statute, and directly shape PSP/vendor roadmaps.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: HTML diff of both the overview and 'popis-okamzitych-plateb' pages; track participant list changes.
queries_used: okamžité platby CERTIS instantní platby povinnost banky termín ČNB SIPS

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Registr pro platby na kontakt (proxy/contact-payment register description)
candidates.why_relevant: Proxy-lookup register attached to CERTIS; its rules/technical annexes create integration obligations for participating PSPs and their core-banking vendors.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching for Visa/Mastercard scheme mandates aimed at CZ acquirers ('mandát', 'pravidla schémat', 'compliance termín') returned no Czech-language scheme-issued rule source. The schemes publish rules only in English; the visa.cz page is a thin consumer-facing pointer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only English scheme rulebooks (visa-rules-public.pdf, mastercard-rules.pdf) and CZ acquirer merchant manuals surfaced; no CZ-language card-scheme rulebook exists as far as the search showed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card-scheme deadlines affecting CZ actors must be tracked in English at source and cross-read against CZ acquirer manuals; a Czech-only monitoring strategy would miss them entirely.

negative_findings.description: No public, CZ-specific compilation of card-scheme mandate calendars (Visa/Mastercard release deadlines as they apply to Czech acquirers/merchants) was found. Trade-press and consultancy blogs (decta, cardcorp, beastinsights) discuss 2026 VAMP and Mastercard scam-merchant rules generically, not for CZ.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only vendor/consultancy commentary, no CZ-scoped mandate calendar.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is a real coverage hole: the deadline calendar must be reconstructed from the global rulebook editions plus acquirer bulletins rather than read off a ready list.

brief: The binding 'payments regulation with a deadline' for Czech actors sits in four distinct rule stacks, each with its own publisher and cadence: ČNB's CERTIS Rules plus the CZK instant-payments scheme (Czech-language, versioned PDFs whose filenames encode effective dates); the EPC's SEPA rulebook family (SCT, SCT Inst, VoP) with formal consultation windows, adherence registers and hard dates such as 15 Nov 2026 for structured addresses and 9 July 2027 for non-euro-area VoP/instant obligations; the card schemes' consolidated public rulebooks (Visa Core Rules, Mastercard Rules), which are English-only and reach CZ actors indirectly through acquirer merchant manuals; and the domestic ČBA COBS open-banking standard plus Bank iD's dated contractual annexes. Coverage is materially asymmetric by language: CERTIS, COBS and Bank iD are Czech-first and well documented, while nothing at the card-scheme layer is published in Czech, so a CZ-only monitoring strategy would silently miss the card mandate calendar. The highest-leverage automated collection targets are the Czech-BA/COBS GitHub repository, the ČNB CERTIS download gallery, the EPC registers of participants filtered to CZ, and periodic hash-diffing of the two scheme rulebook PDFs.
